title: Write a NetworkPolicy
intro: tutorial-010 taught you how to read an existing NetworkPolicy with get/describe. Writing one means correctly telling apart two selectors that look similar but mean opposite things.

steps.prompt: Write a NetworkPolicy named 'deny-from-other' that applies to pods labeled app=db, allowing ingress traffic only from pods labeled app=web.
steps.hint: spec.podSelector (top level) picks which pods this policy applies TO (app=db). spec.ingress[].from[].podSelector picks who's ALLOWED to reach them (app=web) — two different selectors, easy to swap by accident.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-from-other
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: web
steps.explanation: Once this applies, pods labeled app=db only accept traffic from pods labeled app=web — everything else that was previously allowed by default now gets dropped, exactly like the deny-from-other policy you read with describe in tutorial-010.
steps.why: Swapping podSelector and the ingress[].from[].podSelector is an easy, silent mistake — the manifest still applies successfully either way, since both are individually valid selectors. It just enforces the exact opposite rule from what you intended, which is a genuinely dangerous kind of bug because nothing errors.
